A.explanation: Dividing $96$ by $40$ gives $2.4$, but this ignores weight and uses mass instead of weight to balance the thrust.

B.explanation: This is too small because the $40 \text{ kg s}^{-1}$ water jet must gain enough momentum per second to support about $940 \text{ N}$ of weight.

C.explanation: Upward thrust $40v$ balances the $96 \text{ kg}$ weight, giving $v$ about $24 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

D.explanation: This is about twice the correct value and would give a thrust of about $1880 \text{ N}$, double the weight to be supported.

hints: Notice the platform is in vertical equilibrium, so the upward force from changing the water momentum must balance the weight of the $96 \text{ kg}$ man plus platform.
Recall that force equals rate of change of momentum, so for a jet the thrust is $(\text{mass per second}) \times (\text{change in velocity})$ for the $40 \text{ kg s}^{-1}$ discharged downwards.
Set $mg = (40 \text{ kg s}^{-1})v$ with $g = 9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ and solve for the exit speed $v$ of the vertical jet.
walkthrough: Identify equilibrium: resultant vertical force is zero, so upward thrust $F$ on the platform equals total weight $W = mg$ of the $96 \text{ kg}$ man and platform.
Calculate the weight: $W = 96 \times 9.81 = 941.8 \text{ N}$, so about $942 \text{ N}$ upward force is needed.

State the momentum rule: the force accelerating the water downwards equals rate of gain of downward momentum, so by Newton's third law the water pushes up on the platform with $F = \frac{\Delta p}{\Delta t} = \frac{\Delta m}{\Delta t} \times v$.
Substitute the mass flow rate: $F = 40 \times v$, where $F$ is in $\text{N}$ when $v$ is in $\text{m s}^{-1}$.
Equate thrust to weight: $40v = 941.8$, so $v = 941.8 / 40 = 23.5 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, which is about $24 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ with sensible precision. This is option C.
